@cli.command()
def new() -> None:
    """
    Create a new Lean blueprint in the given repository.
    """
    assert lakefile is not None
    loader = FileSystemLoader(Path(__file__).parent/"templates")
    env = Environment(loader=loader, variable_start_string='{|', variable_end_string='|}',
                      comment_start_string='{--', comment_end_string='--}')

    console.print("\nWelcome to Lean blueprint\n", style="title")
    can_try_ci = True

    if repo is None:
        error("Could not find a Lean project. Please run this command from inside your project folder.")

    if repo.is_dirty():
        error("The repository contains uncommitted changes. Please clean it up before creating a blueprint.")

    # Will now try to guess the author name
    try:
        name = repo.git.config("user.name")
    except GitCommandError:
        try:
            # Name of the author of the first commit.
            name = deque(repo.iter_commits(), 1)[0].author.name
        except (IndexError, ValueError):
            # This will happen if there is no commit in the repo.
            name = "Anonymous"


    libs = lakefile.parse_libs()
    if not libs:
        warning(
            "Could not find Lean library names in lakefile. Will not propose to setup continuous integration.")
        can_try_ci = False

    manifest_path = Path(repo.working_dir)/"lake-manifest.json"

    # Will now try to guess the GitHub url
    github = ""
    githubIO = ""
    doc_home = ""
    githubUserName = ""
    githubRepoName = ""
    try:
        url = repo.remote().url
    except ValueError:
        url = None
    if url:
        patterns = [r"https://github.com/(.*)/(.*)\.git",
                    r"https://github.com/(.*)/(.*)",
                    r"git@github.com:(.*)/(.*)\.git",
                    r"git@github.com:(.*)/(.*)"]
        m = next(m for m in map(lambda p: re.match(p, url), patterns) if m is not None)
        if m:
            githubUserName = m.group(1)
            githubRepoName = m.group(2)
        if githubUserName:
            github = f"https://github.com/{githubUserName}/{githubRepoName}"
            githubIO = f"https://{githubUserName}.github.io/{githubRepoName}"
            doc_home = f"https://{githubUserName}.github.io/{githubRepoName}/docs"
        else:
            warning(
                "Could not guess GitHub information. Will not propose to setup continuous integration.")
            can_try_ci = False

    out_dir = Path(repo.working_dir)/"blueprint"
    if out_dir.exists():
        error("There is already a blueprint folder. Aborting blueprint creation.")

    console.print("We will now ask some questions to configure your blueprint. All answers can be changed later by editing either the plastex.cfg file or the tex files.")
    config: Dict[str, Any] = dict()

    12	/-!
    13	# The identity component of the Picard scheme
    14	
    15	Let `G` be a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type. Its **identity
    16	component** `G⁰` is the connected component of `|G|` containing the image of
    17	the identity section. It is an open and closed subgroup scheme of `G`, of
    18	finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`, and its formation
    19	commutes with extension of the base field (Kleiman, §5, Lem.~`lem:agps`).
    20	
    21	This file develops that substrate for an arbitrary `k`-group scheme (§1) and
    22	then specialises it to the conditional legacy `PicSharp` representer
    23	`PicScheme C` (§2). Section §3 contains only candidate integer maps at the
    24	trivial legacy test object; it does not construct the arbitrary-test degree on
    25	the étale-sheafified Picard functor. The corresponding degree-zero
    26	characterisation in §4 remains open and is not faithfully typed by its legacy
    27	approximation.
    28	
    29	## Main results
    30	
    31	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` — the identity component
    32	  `G⁰` of a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of finite type, as a `k`-scheme (an
    33	  object of `Over (Spec k)`): the open subscheme of `G` carried by the
    34	  connected component of the image of the identity section.
    35	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme` —
    36	  the inclusion `G⁰ ↪ G` is both an open and a closed immersion.
    37	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism` —
    38	  `G⁰` inherits the group-object structure of `G`.
    39	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso` — for a
    40	  field extension `K/k`, the base change `(G⁰)_K` is isomorphic to `(G_K)⁰`.
    41	- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`
    42	  — `G⁰` is of finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`.
    43	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme` — the identity component
    44	  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the Picard scheme.
    45	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.degree` — a conditional totalisation of
    46	  an additive candidate at the legacy trivial test object, available only from
    47	  `[ClassDegreePinned C]` and set arbitrarily to `0` off sections.
    48	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus` — the dimension of
    49	  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is the genus of `C`.
    50	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree` — the current
    51	  conditional, typed-sorry approximation to the degree-zero characterisation;
    52	  it is not an exact encoding of the classical statement on `k`-points.
    53	
    54	The abelian-variety identification of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (smooth, proper,
    55	geometrically irreducible `k`-group scheme of dimension `g(C)`) is assembled
    56	in the sibling file `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`.
    57	
    58	## Remaining obligations
    59	
    60	The §1 substrate for an abstract `k`-group scheme is unconditional. The open
    61	residues downstream of arbitrary-field étale Picard representability are
    62	mathematically distinct:
    63	
    64	- a genuine signed family degree: an additive natural transformation whose
    65	  fibre value is `χ(C_t, L_t) - χ(C_t, O_{C_t})`, locally constant on arbitrary
    66	  test schemes and invariant under the relative Picard quotient. The existing
    67	  `ClassDegreePinned` interface does not provide these properties.
    68	- `Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus`: the equality
    69	  `dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = dim_k H¹(C, O_C) = g(C)`, which follows from
    70	  Picard smoothness plus the tangent-space/dimension comparison. It does not
    71	  depend on extracting a representing line bundle from a `k`-point.
    72	- `Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree`: the identification of the `k`-points of
    73	  the legacy `Pic⁰_{C/k}` approximation with candidate-value-zero classes;
    74	  its current type is not the arbitrary-field mathematical statement.
    75	
    76	## References
    77	
    78	- Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_IdentityComponent.tex`.
    79	- Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, Lem.~`lem:agps` (identity component
    80	  substrate) + Prp.~`prp:pic0` (specialisation to `Pic_{C/k}`) +
    81	  Thm.~`th:qpp&p` (quasi-projectivity/projectivity) + Cor.~`cor:sm`
    82	  (smoothness/dimension) + Ex.~`ex:jac` + Rmk.~`rmk:Jac`
    83	  (arXiv:math/0504020 pp. 36, 38, 47, 50–51);
    84	- Milne, "Abelian Varieties" (course notes, 2008), §III.1
    85	  (def. of abelian variety, p. 8; dimension equals genus, Rmk. III.1.4(e),
    86	  p. 86).
    87	-/

That is the whole reason\n   395\tthis direction is worth having as a separate lemma. -/\n   396\ttheorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]\n   397\t    (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by\n   398\t  intro s hs\n   399\t  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)\n   400\t  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx => hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩\n   401\t\n   730\t  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := hU (U.ι.base ⁻¹' s) (hs.preimage U.ι.isOpenEmbedding.injective.injOn)\n   731\t  refine ⟨⟨U.ι ''ᵁ W.1, W.2.image_of_isOpenImmersion U.ι⟩, ?_⟩\n   732\t  intro x hx\n   733\t  exact ⟨⟨x, hsub hx⟩, hW (by simpa using hx), rfl⟩\n   734\t\n   735\t/-- **The piecewise form of §3**: a finite set contained in an open subscheme that is\n   736\tprojective over an affine base lies in an affine open of the ambient scheme.\n   737\t\n   738\tComposing §6.1 with §3. theorem fgaPicardRepresentability {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    (∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom)
      ∧ (HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=

/-- **The étale representability gate**, as a `Prop`-class so that consumers can
quantify over it as a hypothesis.

applied; there is no `C` in the domain for which the binder is a real

the binder genuinely is a hypothesis. What this class does buy is the shape:
statements quantified over it read as implications and are stated for an
arbitrary base field, per `I-0491`. See `PicSchemeEt` below for the
measurement. -/
class HasPicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where
  has_pic_scheme_et : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
    Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom

curve, with no rational-point hypothesis — which is the whole content of the
owner decision of 2026-07-28. Its mathematics is

    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : HasPicSchemeEt C :=

/-- **THE ASSEMBLY.** A `k`-scheme `Y` whose points are naturally the
cover-compatible `picEt C`-classes on `T_{k'}` REPRESENTS `picEt C`.

noncomputable def representableBy_of_coverCompatibleEquiv
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    {Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
    (e : ∀ T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)), (T ⟶ Y) ≃ CoverCompatible (k' := k') C T)
    (he : ∀ {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (f : T ⟶ T') (g : T' ⟶ Y),
      (e T (f ≫ g)).1 = ((coverFunctor (k := k) (k' := k')).op ⋙ picEt C).map f.op (e T' g).1) :
    (picEt C).RepresentableBy Y where
  homEquiv {T} := (e T).trans (restrictCompatEquiv (k' := k') C T).symm
  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f g := by
    apply (restrictCompatEquiv (k' := k') C T).injective
    change (restrictCompatEquiv (k' := k') C T)
        ((restrictCompatEquiv (k' := k') C T).symm (e T (f ≫ g))) = _
    rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    rw [restrictCompatEquiv_naturality (k' := k') C f]
    change (e T (f ≫ g)).1 = ((coverFunctor (k := k) (k' := k')).op ⋙ picEt C).map f.op
      ((restrictCompatEquiv (k' := k') C T')
        ((restrictCompatEquiv (k' := k') C T').symm (e T' g))).1
    rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    exact he f g

/-- **THE CONVERSE — so the assembly is a CHANGE OF COORDINATES, not a
strengthening, and this file says so as a theorem rather than as a caveat.**

A representation of `picEt C` by `Y` yields exactly the data
`representableBy_of_coverCompatibleEquiv` consumes: the per-test `Equiv` *and* its
naturality. Composed with that theorem, the two are **inter-derivable**.

This is the check a "reduction" claim owes before publication. Both directions are
proved, so the honest description of the assembly is: *to represent `picEt C` it is
equivalent to represent the cover-compatible-classes functor*. That is a genuine
repricing — the right-hand side is what a Galois quotient of a `k'`-side
representation produces, and the left-hand side is clause (1) field 1 — but it is
**not** a discount on the seam and must not be reported as one. -/
noncomputable def coverCompatibleEquiv_of_representableBy
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    {Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
    (rep : (picEt C).RepresentableBy Y) :
    Σ' e : ∀ T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)), (T ⟶ Y) ≃ CoverCompatible (k' := k') C T,
      ∀ {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (f : T ⟶ T') (g : T' ⟶ Y),
        (e T (f ≫ g)).1
          = ((coverFunctor (k := k) (k' := k')).op ⋙ picEt C).map f.op (e T' g).1 :=
  ⟨fun T => rep.homEquiv.trans (restrictCompatEquiv (k' := k') C T), by
    intro T T' f g
    change (picEt C).map (coverMap (k' := k') T).op (rep.homEquiv (f ≫ g)) = _
    rw [rep.homEquiv_comp]
    exact restrictCompatEquiv_naturality (k' := k') C f (rep.homEquiv g)⟩

/-- A class on `T_{k'}` fixed by every `γ ∈ Gal(k'/k)`, in `ajc-p1`'s `twistTest`
spelling. -/
def IsGalInvariant (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (x : (picEt C).obj (op ((coverFunctor (k := k) (k' := k')).obj T))) : Prop :=
  ∀ γ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k',

/-- **`IsCoverCompatible` implies `IsGalInvariant`, unconditionally** — `ajc-p1`'s
`invariant_of_projections_agree`, in this file's predicate spelling. -/
theorem isGalInvariant_of_isCoverCompatible (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    {x : (picEt C).obj (op ((coverFunctor (k := k) (k' := k')).obj T))}

def GalInvariant (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) : Type (u + 1) :=

    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (hcov : Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows

  toFun x := ⟨x.1, isGalInvariant_of_isCoverCompatible C T x.2⟩
  invFun x := ⟨x.1, isCoverCompatible_of_isGalInvariant C T hcov x.2⟩

    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    {Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
    (hcov : ∀ T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)), Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows
        (fun _ : k' ≃ₐ[k] k' => (restrictTest k k').obj (baseTest (k' := k') T))
        (fun γ => coverSelfSection T γ)) ∈

        (coverMap (k := k) (k' := k') T)))
    (e : ∀ T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)), (T ⟶ Y) ≃ GalInvariant (k' := k') C T)
    (he : ∀ {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (f : T ⟶ T') (g : T' ⟶ Y),
      (e T (f ≫ g)).1 = ((coverFunctor (k := k) (k' := k')).op ⋙ picEt C).map f.op (e T' g).1) :

+/-!
+# Rational points of schemes over fields
+
+This module isolates the lightweight predicate that a scheme over a field has a
+section. Keeping it below the Picard representability development lets geometric
+base-change modules use the predicate without importing the FGA seam.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
+
+/-- **`C` has a `k`-rational point**: the structural morphism `C.hom` admits a
+section `sigma : Spec k ⟶ C.left`. For the smooth proper geometrically integral
+curves of this project this is the pointing already threaded through the
+Albanese statements.
+
+This is a predicate only. In particular, this module provides no instance that
+would manufacture a rational point for an arbitrary curve. -/
+class HasRationalPoint {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Prop where
+  nonempty_section :
+    Nonempty {sigma : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left // sigma ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))}
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
